unit.label: Extant copying on the P52 leaf
unit.reason: Hurtado describes the extant recto and verso as one fragment and discusses the scribe of both sides as a single copyist; no separate correction or supplement is identified in this bounded review.

CSNTM, Manuscript P52, manuscript details, https://manuscripts.csntm.org/manuscript/Group/GA_P52; consulted 2026-09-29. Broad century label without an explicitly stated inclusive interval.

Brent Nongbri, 'Palaeography, Precision and Publicity: Further Thoughts on P.Ryl. iii.457 (P52)', New Testament Studies 66.4 (2020), pp. 471-499, abstract, https://doi.org/10.1017/S0028688520000089; consulted 2026-09-29. The accessible abstract argues for a wider possible range but supplies no inclusive numeric bounds.

Don Barker, 'The Dating of New Testament Papyri', New Testament Studies 57.4 (2011), pp. 573-574, especially p. 574, https://research-management.mq.edu.au/ws/portalfiles/portal/62382986/Publisher%2Bversion%2B%28open%2Baccess%29.pdf; consulted 2026-09-29. Barker's full argument assigns P.Ryl. 457 to the second or third century. Bounds 101-300 CE normalize those complete centuries; they are not measured endpoints or a consensus date.

selection.reason: Barker's full argument supplies a broad second-or-third-century assessment, but an independent human review of the physical evidence and dating interpretation is still pending. The narrower NTVMR 125-175 catalogue interval remains unselected; no date is selected for ranking.
